uncited: *   **Inputs:** A set of training views $\{v\}$ with ground truth images $\{I^v\}$ at full resolution; a camera model for each view.
*   **Gaussian Field $G^\ell$:** A set of $N_\ell$ anisotropic Gaussian primitives.
*   Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients for view-dependent color.
*   **Error Accumulation:** Training each field to directly match its Laplacian residual target ($R^\ell$) can lead to accumulated approximation errors and degraded quality.
*   **Time Complexity:** Reduces training time by optimizing fewer Gaussians per stage and reducing per-iteration cost at coarser levels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Significantly reduces peak VRAM usage by archiving completed Gaussian fields off the GPU.
*   **Strengths:** Efficient training for high-resolution scenes; reduced memory footprint; leverages standard 3DGS densification/pruning.
*   **Limitations:** Slight quality drop; deeper hierarchies may degrade quality; requires careful tuning of inheritance ratio $\rho$ if speed is prioritized over quality.
*   **When to Use:** When training time or VRAM is a bottleneck for high-resolution 3DGS scenes.
*   **When Not to Use:** When maximum reconstruction fidelity is required and training time is not a constraint.

It builds on the observation that low-frequency structures in 3DGS converge earlier than high-frequency details, and that standard 3DGS rasterizers assume non-negative colors, which is incompatible with signed residual learning.
